author: Kevin Kelly
short: Native music with short-song caching, playlists, player panels and daily checks.
description: Music search and playback inside Red using yt-dlp, FFmpeg, and native Discord voice with DAVE support. Includes direct play/skip/queue commands and matching slash controls. Joins your voice channel, or the available voice channel with the most people if you are not in voice. Disconnects after the queue is idle for 10 seconds. No Lavalink server is needed. Install PyNaCl>=1.5.0,<1.6 and davey>=0.1.6 once in Red's Python environment, plus FFmpeg, libopus, and Deno 2.3+ or Node.js 22+ in the Red container. Working voice libraries from Downloader remain supported. Unload Red's bundled Audio cog before loading AudioPlus. Optional owner-configured daily checks test silent YouTube playback in Discord and DM the configuring owner on failure, postponing existing voice sessions. Includes checked automatic player panels, seek and queue editing, saved member playlists/favorites, and opt-in DJ/vote policies with guided setup. Adds requester-only search selection, opt-in round-robin fair queues, and bounded artist-based autoplay. Owner-only audiorepair reinstalls missing, unimportable, or incompatible native voice libraries in Red's Python environment and verifies required APIs in a fresh process before a required restart. Native checks include Discord's cached library bindings and catch a missing davey.DAVE_PROTOCOL_VERSION before connecting. Daily failure alerts identify the failing stage and safe exception details; audiostatus retains the last monitored-server result after the probe disconnects. Optional queue recovery, empty-room pause/departure, volume normalization and collaborative server playlists with DJ approvals. Adds bounded listening history, stable-ID replay and atomic duration/per-member request limits with DJ exemptions. Add opt-in disconnect session summaries with decoded playback time, recent tracks, requester counts, three-minute playlist saving controls and transient identified-user data hooks. Optional IntroPlus shares a native connection lock, cancels temporary intro voice sessions on play, and overlays bounded entrance clips over active same-channel PCM music without changing the queue or progress. Automatically caches known non-live provider songs strictly under five minutes as server-scoped local audio copies for three calendar months, with a 2 GiB/2,000-song bot-wide limit, bounded background preparation, cache status/clear controls and requester privacy cleanup. Daily YouTube probes bypass cached audio.
install_msg: Read https://github.com/kevinwaynekelly/kevin-cogs/blob/main/audioplus/README.md before loading. Downloader installs yt-dlp and EJS. Native voice also requires PyNaCl>=1.5.0,<1.6 and davey>=0.1.6, installed once in Red's Python environment; cog updates keep existing voice libraries. Install FFmpeg, libopus, and a supported JavaScript runtime inside the Red container. If PyNaCl or davey cannot import or reports incompatible native APIs, the bot owner can run [p]audiorepair with voice disconnected. It repairs failing voice libraries in Red's Python environment; restart Red after the repair result, then run [p]audiostatus. Repair does not install FFmpeg, Opus, or a JavaScript runtime. Unload Red's bundled Audio cog first if loaded. Use [p]audiostatus to check local dependencies, then [p]play <query>. Play joins your voice channel, or the available channel with the most people, and leaves after the queue is idle for 10 seconds. For slash commands, the owner runs [p]slash enablecog audioplus and [p]slash sync after loading. Legacy [p]audio commands remain available. No Lavalink node is required. Optional: run [p]audiocheck enable in your server for daily checks at 09:00 America/Chicago and private failure alerts, then [p]audiocheck now for an immediate silent test. Eligible short songs cache automatically for three calendar months. Use [p]audiocache or /audiocache status for usage; Red administrators or Manage Server can clear copies. Cache files use the persistent AudioPlus data directory and require FFmpeg with libopus plus FFprobe. Sync slash commands after updating.
end_user_data_statement: Preserves legacy Lavalink connection settings, including the node password, in Red Config for rollback. Native playback ignores them. Optional daily checks store the configuring owner's Discord ID, test server/channel IDs, public video URL, local schedule, latest safe result, and pending failure DM in Config. User-data hooks export or remove that owner's check settings and disable the monitor. Request contexts are transient. Optional recovery stores up to 100 public track records, requester IDs, position, pause state, volume and repeat mode for seven days, checkpointed every ten seconds and on clean unload. Intentional stop/disconnect clears active checkpoints. Guild settings store music panel/DJ/vote preferences and member-specific playlists/favorites with source URLs and metadata; Shared server playlists retain up to ten collections of 100 approved tracks and 100 suggestions, with proposer IDs. User-data hooks export/delete personal collections, remove pending suggestions and anonymize approved/recovery requester attribution. Listening history starts enabled and stores up to 100 public playback-start records per server for 30 days, capped at 512 KiB, with requester IDs, times and metadata. Members can clear their own records; administrators can disable/erase history. User-data hooks export/delete identified request records. No extracted signed stream URL, provider credentials or yt-dlp disk cache is persisted. Opt-in session summaries retain up to 100 public track starts, requester IDs and decoded playback time per active connection in bounded memory. Up to 20 completed summaries and save controls remain in memory for three minutes; export/deletion hooks include these identified requests. Saving a session uses the existing personal playlist storage. Posted summaries remain on Discord; unload clears transient session records. Local song caching starts automatically on upgrade. Known non-live provider tracks strictly under five minutes are copied as audio-only Opus files in AudioPlus's persistent cog data directory, separately scoped by server. Copies expire three calendar months after download, without extending on replay. Storage is capped at 2 GiB and 2,000 songs across the bot, with a 16 MiB per-copy limit. Cache metadata stores server IDs, hashed public source URLs, duration, size, creation time and up to 128 requester IDs per song; additional requesters create no cache attribution record. No source titles, raw URLs, signed streams, or HTTP headers are saved in cache metadata. User-data hooks export identified cache metadata and delete whole copies associated with that user, including shared copies, while cancelling associated downloads. Manage Server or Red administrators can clear their server's cache; server removal also erases its copies. Complete copies survive reload/restart, while owned downloads and partial files are cancelled/removed.
